claude-modeling-skills

Claude Code skills for making 3D game content with measured gates instead of "looks right" verdicts. Five skills share one idea: every phase has to pass numeric checks (dimensions, silhouettes, triangle budgets, validators, headless engine renders) before the next one starts, and a separate fresh-eyes critic reviews the result with no stake in calling it done.

Skill What it makes Proves it with
reference-modeling real-world objects in Blender from reference images dimension and silhouette gates, extent profiles, mesh report
game-asset-modeling engine-ready glTF: kit pieces, props, vehicles, weapons, decals, characters triangle budgets, UV checks, the Khronos validator, Babylon review renders
game-animation game clips from open motion capture on a shared skeleton, incl. first-person sets loop seams, foot slide, joint limits, engine playback
game-vfx particle effects as portable JSON plus painted flipbook sheets schema and budget validation, overdraw and frame-strip review
game-ui icon sets, nine-slice panels, templates, design tokens, licensed fonts palette and legibility gates, headless review at game size

The four game-* skills were built for one project (an asymmetric police-state game with a Babylon web console and a Godot first-person client) and carry its conventions in their references; the pipelines, validators and review harnesses are general.

reference-modeling

Model real-world objects in Blender from reference images, aiming for accurate proportions, correct 3D form and clean topology rather than a stack of boxes or a flat extruded slab. Claude drives a live Blender session through the BlenderMCP server. Every phase has to pass numeric gates before the next one starts:

Gate What it checks
dim_gate Each part's measured spans against real dimensions (±5 %)
silhouette_iou Rendered silhouette against a filled reference mask, per view (≥ 0.90)
extent_profile Cross-section width sampled along the part, which catches the "uniform slab" failure
landmark_delta Interior features that no silhouette shows
mesh_report ngons, non-manifold edges, loose verts

What's in it

skills/reference-modeling/
├── SKILL.md                       # the workflow: phases 0–5, gates, critique loop, gotchas
├── references/
│   ├── edit-mode-techniques.md    # profile extrusion, loft/bridge form pass, booleans, bmesh
│   ├── sdf-molded-parts.md        # rounded/molded parts from side-view fields (marching cubes)
│   └── materials-and-rendering.md # scale-aware lighting, procedural materials, render setup
└── scripts/
    ├── (run inside Blender via MCP)
    │   set_ortho_view · silhouette_metrics · silhouette_iou · extent_profile · landmark
    │   mesh_report · symmetry · bevel · finish_shading · zoom_region · add_reference
    │   blender_ref · import_npz
    └── (run offline in CPython)
        trace_profile.py   # photo → filled mask → calibrated world-space contours
        sdf_mesher.py      # side-view width/radius/squareness fields → smooth solid (.npz)

Workflow in brief

  1. Research and set up. Find orthographic references (blueprints, patent drawings, or a square-on product photo) and pin down the real dimensions. Choose a construction strategy (revolve, mirror, array or freeform) from what the references show. Calibrate the image to true scale and build a filled silhouette mask for each view.
  2. Blockout with primitives until the proportions pass dim_gate.
  3. Primary silhouette. No new primitives from here on. Use edit-mode profile extrusion traced from the mask. For molded parts, use the SDF inflate method instead.
  4. 3D form. Add loop cuts at section changes, set the envelope, shape cross-sections with loft/bridge, and gate with extent_profile.
  5. Detail. Align booleans to the reference before cutting, then clean up afterwards.
  6. Final QA. Re-run every gate, add limited bevels with weighted normals, apply materials, and render beauty shots.

Install

git clone git@github.com:colinurbs/claude-modeling-skills.git
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
for s in reference-modeling game-asset-modeling game-animation game-vfx game-ui; do
  ln -s "$PWD/claude-modeling-skills/skills/$s" ~/.claude/skills/$s
done
# the game skills' review and validation tooling (Babylon, Playwright, the Khronos validator)
sh ~/.claude/skills/game-asset-modeling/tools/setup.sh

Code blocks in the skills load helpers from ~/.claude/skills/<skill>/scripts and .../tools. If you install a skill elsewhere (for example a project's .claude/skills/), update that path. The game-* skills read a project's assets/spec.json, ASSETS.md and assets/manifest.json for budgets, naming and delivery status; see each SKILL.md.

Requirements

  • Blender 4.x–5.x. reference-modeling needs the BlenderMCP add-on running (sidebar N → BlenderMCP → Start) and the BlenderMCP server configured in Claude Code; the game-* skills drive Blender headless from the command line. Tested on Blender 5.1.
  • Node 20+ for the game skills' tooling (tools/setup.sh installs it).
  • For the offline helpers, run pip install -r requirements.txt (numpy, scipy, pillow, opencv-python-headless, scikit-image).
  • Web access, so Claude can find reference images.

Usage

Ask Claude Code something like:

model a Stanley No. 4 hand plane in Blender from references, as realistic as you can

build the delivery truck from ASSETS.md as a static blocker, with LODs and a collider

retarget this CMU walk onto our skeleton as a seamless loop with root motion

make the muzzle flash and the tear-gas volume for the riot launcher

design the dossier template and the unit icon set for the control room

Each skill triggers on its own kind of request; the descriptions in the SKILL.md frontmatter say what counts.

Honest limits

The gates make sure a model isn't grossly wrong, and they stop premature "looks right" verdicts. They don't guarantee beauty. Subtle compound curvature and fine surface detail still take iteration, and whether a bevel radius "reads as steel" is still a judgment call.

Covers the whole pipeline: asset brief, pl
